content.text:
I've submitted **index 9 (V 0.858, Zr 0.142)** as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured: 7.58 µA. The 16 compositions run from V 0.26 to V 0.88, and I only had three merit measurements, so this is the best measured point rather than a proven library optimum.

| Index | V fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.673 (close to the ZrV₂O₇ compound) | 0.23 µA |
| 0 | 0.881 (the most V-rich composition) | 3.73 µA |
| 9 | 0.858 | 7.58 µA |

- **How I chose:** The only mixed V–Zr compound checked, ZrV₂O₇, came out stable. Its predicted band gap is 2.7–3.1 eV, depending on the method, which is close to the 3.22 eV light. V₂O₅ is also stable and has a lower gap.
- **What the results show:** Photocurrent rises sharply toward the V-rich end, where the film should be a mix of ZrV₂O₇ and V₂O₅. It then drops again at the V-rich edge, so the peak is probably around V ≈ 0.85.
- **What was left unmeasured:** Index 12 (V 0.83) could be as good as or better than index 9. The trend model's top suggestion for the last measurement was index 4 (V 0.80), but I picked index 9 instead. The Zr-rich compositions were never measured; I expect them to be poor because ZrO₂ shouldn't absorb 3.22 eV light.
- **Not used:** I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase mix at each composition is inferred, not confirmed.
